claim: Shear pin rating 302 N nominal (256 to 347 N) from 2.0 mm soft aluminium wire in double shear
law: Double shear, F = 2 tau A; tau about 0.6 x tensile strength (von Mises); O-temper 1050 about 80 MPa tensile
check: 48 MPa (assumed) gives 302 N; 1100-O at a handbook 62 MPa gives 390 N, above the top of the band (347 N); half-hard or hard-drawn wire is far above it. The 1 mm gaps either side of the tang add bending and bearing (about 29 MPa on the tang), so the rating holds only for an O-temper reel calibrated on CalRig in a fork and tang like the real ones (PR-011). The plus or minus 15 % band is a requirement, not a result

claim: Every load path except the pin is at least twice as strong as the pin (smallest margin: pole buckling)
law: Euler buckling of the pinned 4.35 m pole, pi^2 E I / L^2, 6063-T6 E 69 GPa; other paths in SMR-CAL-001 Table 4

claim: Hook head J stays at least twice as strong as the pin with the bight in the bottom of the J
law: Curved bar in bending, sigma = Kc M / Z + F / A, Wahl inner-fibre factor Kc = (4C - 1) / (4C - 4); S235 yield 235 MPa. The 10 mm bar of SMR-DDR-003 gave a factor of 1.86 (Fails, fix proposed); fixed with 12 mm bar (SMR-DEC-001 F1)

claim: A net hooked over a branch (half a turn) lifts off below the low end of the pin band
law: Capstan (Euler-Eytelwein) T1 = T2 e^(mu theta) + crew line; friction of wet netting on wet bark 0.3 to 0.5 and a 20 N far leg assumed (SMR-CAL-001 A6, A7)
check: 126 N against 256 N (margin 2.0); the margin is gone at a far-leg tension of 47 N or a friction of about 0.8 (independent review). The law is standard, its inputs are assumptions
closed_by: SMR-CAL-001 s4 [F2, F5, F9] on assumed inputs; staged-snag trials at TRL 4

claim: The hook head works a wrapped net back round the branch half a turn at a time within the pin band
law: Capstan: each half turn worked back divides the far-leg term by e^(mu pi) = 2.6 to 4.8; the drag the hook needs depends on how the net lies
check: Lift after one half turn back 162 to 493 N against 256 N; the hook's own drag cannot be set on paper

claim: Static heel of the design canoe when the pin breaks at the top of its band, kneeling, is under 5 deg
law: Righting moment = displacement x g x GM x sin(heel); GM from waterplane inertia (0.05 L B^3) and mass centres (SMR-CAL-001 A2 to A5)
check: 3.41 deg against 5 deg on screening hydrostatics; 5.1 deg with a 1.0 m beam, 4.7 deg with a 0.04 waterplane factor, 7.4 deg with both (independent review). Met only once GM is measured
closed_by: SMR-CAL-001 s3 [H5, H6, Q1 to Q3] on screening hydrostatics; moored heel test at TRL 4

claim: With the steady-lift rule, a quick pull does not take the design canoe past the 5 deg static limit; the peak under a jerk is measured at TRL 4
law: Undamped roll oscillator, period 2 pi k / sqrt(g GM) = 1.06 s (k = 0.40 B); a pull rising in 0.25 s overshoots by 1 + |sin x| / x = 1.91
check: Peak 6.5 deg kneeling for a pull held just under the pin; if the pin breaks at the top of the ramp the heel then is only 33 % of static (independent review). Decided by Amish on 2026-10-25 (SMR-DEC-001 O6, option A): the 2.0 mm pin stays, 5 deg is the static limit, "lift steadily, never jerk" is an operating rule and on the tag, and the moored heel test measures the roll period and the jerk peak; a 1.7 mm pin only if that test shows a real exceedance

claim: With the crew still holding 100 N on the line as the pin breaks at the top of its band, the design canoe heels under 5 deg
law: As S6, with the line tension over the crutch added; the line tension that alone takes the heel to 5 deg is 203 N
closed_by: SMR-CAL-001 s3 [H14, H15]; operating rule: slacken the line when the operator lifts

claim: Canoes under 7 m must be excluded: a 5.5 m dugout heels past 5 deg before the pin breaks
law: As S6, for the 5.5 m two-crew dugout (SMR-CAL-001 A3)

claim: Hook head J stays at least twice as strong as the pin if the bight catches on the tip leg
law: As S3 with the arm doubled (60 mm, the tip leg); no yield before the pin breaks while the factor is above 1
check: Factor 1.58 with 12 mm bar (independent review). Fixes (14 mm bar, about 0.09 kg more, so the bamboo variant's carried mass passes 4 kg; or a welded gusset) trade PR-007, so they went to Amish (SMR-DEC-001 O10). He approved the gusset on 2026-10-25, but the straight shank above the bend carries the same moment at a factor of 1.87, which a gusset at the bend does not reach, and a gusset to the flat breaks PR-007; back with Amish (docs/REVIEW.md)

claim: The aluminium pole does not yield under the largest side couple a kneeling operator can apply
law: Tube bending, M = 200 N per hand x 0.6 m between the hands (A13), against the 214 MPa proof of 6063-T6; the pin does not cap side loads

claim: Accepted bamboo culms (bend test) do not buckle before the pin breaks in a push
law: Euler buckling of the bamboo pole at E 15 GPa, the stiffness the bend test accepts; under the 2 x rule of PR-012, which Amish's variant decision of SMR-DDR-003 already records
closed_by: SMR-CAL-001 s10 [V5, V10]; PR-012 at risk for the bamboo pole

claim: Top hand to ring is at least 4 m with three 1.45 m sections
law: Geometry of cad/src/model.py (derived hand_to_ring)

claim: The float winder floats a dropped ring and tether with a reserve above 1
law: Archimedes: foam lift (1000 - 30 kg/m3) against the weight in water of steel and polyester

claim: Hot-dip galvanised steel parts show no functional corrosion after 6 months stored wet in fresh water
law: Zinc coatings to ISO 1461 (mean 55 to 85 um by steel thickness) corrode slowly in fresh water; zinc is anodic to steel and protects cut edges
check: Coating life far exceeds 6 months in fresh water; the field check (PR-008) confirms in the canoe bottom
closed_by: SMR-CAL-001 A8; PR-008 field check at TRL 4

claim: Stainless pins and rivets in the aluminium pole and the aluminium pin in galvanised steel do not seize or pit in fresh water
law: Galvanic series (ASTM G82 guide): zinc is anodic to aluminium, which is anodic to stainless steel; fresh water's low conductivity limits the current
check: Mild couples; aluminium round the stainless pins and rivets is the part at risk. Confirmed only by the 6 month wet storage check

claim: Borax and boric acid treated bamboo (local variant) does not rot or attract borers in 6 months wet
law: Boron salts are standard bamboo preservatives against fungi and insects but leach in wet service
check: Leaching in a wet canoe bottom is the risk; the field check decides

claim: A kneeling operator can lift 126 N on the pole to free a hooked net
law: Comparable to lifting a 15 L bucket of water (147 N), a load carried routinely at landing sites

claim: Whole kit mass from the calculation note agrees with the detailed CAD model
law: Sum of part volumes x densities in cad/fidelity.json (foam taken at 120 kg/m3 there, 30 in CAL)

claim: Pins cut from one reel break within plus or minus 15 % of the rating
law: Wire diameter tolerance of about 0.03 mm on 2.0 mm is about 3 % of area; strength scatter within one reel of O-temper wire is usually smaller than between reels
check: Ten pins broken per reel on CalRig decide (TRL 4)

claim: A village smith bends 12 mm bar to a 112 mm mean diameter within 2 mm over a former
law: Cold bending of 12 mm mild steel round over a turned former is routine blacksmith work; springback is taken out by overbending
check: Checked against a full-size template at the build (SMR-BLD-001); the 2 mm joint gap absorbs small errors

claim: Option B: a 2.2 kg knocker dropped 0.5 m along the line strikes with about 10 J
law: Energy of the weight in water, speed capped at its terminal speed (3.7 m/s, Cd about 1)

claim: Option B: knocks along the near leg of the line free a net draped over a branch
law: Angling lure retrievers free a hook by knocking the lure back along the line; a net over a branch has no hook point, and a knock along the near leg pushes the bight down onto the branch
check: Not shown on paper; expected to work only on light snags. Kept as option A's deep-snag mode (jigging weight on the tang)

claim: Option B: jigging the knocker heels the design canoe less than 1 deg
law: Line tension three times the weight in water at the crutch, 0.6 m arm, against the righting moment of S6

claim: Option C: the shear link caps the rope pull at the same band as option A
law: The same 2.0 mm soft aluminium pin in double shear in a fork and tang link
closed_by: SMR-CAL-001 s2, s3 (pull for 5 deg kneeling)

claim: Option C: a grapnel tine loaded at its tip is at least twice as strong as the link
law: Cantilever tine, 14 mm bar, 60 mm arm, sigma = M / Z against S235 yield. With 12 mm tines the factor was 1.91 (Fails, fix proposed; independent review); 14 mm tines (SMR-DEC-001 F2)

claim: Option C: pulling the net from the opposite side unwinds a wrap
law: Capstan: a pull in the unwinding direction meets the crew-side tension times e^(mu theta) and each half turn undone divides it by 2.6 to 4.8
check: Plausible; needs a second canoe or an anchored float, and the grapnel may bite the tree instead of the net
